# RAG and retrieval

English · [Русский](../ru/themes/rag-retrieval.md) · ← [AI Interview Atlas](../../README.md)

Grounding answers in documents: chunking, hybrid search, reranking, permissions, freshness and citation.

## Both tracks

- **When should a retrieval application plan multiple searches instead of making one fixed retrieval call?**
  - Knowledge
  - Tests: Whether iterative retrieval earns its extra cost and failure modes.
- **Design retrieval that enforces the source system's access rights, including permission changes and shared caches.**
  - System design · Asked at: [Databricks](../companies/databricks.md) †, [Microsoft](../companies/microsoft.md) †, [Palantir](../companies/palantir.md) †
  - Tests: Whether access checks cover the full path to generated output.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Propagate identity and enforce authorisation before content reaches the model.
    - Keep permission updates, deletions and cache keys consistent with the policy.
    - Test denied access and revocation paths; citations and logs need the same boundary.
  - Read: [Document-level access control](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/search-document-level-access-overview) (Microsoft Learn)

## AI Engineering

- **Choose a chunking approach for technical documentation, including how you preserve meaning across section boundaries.**
  - Applied scenario
  - Tests: Whether chunk size follows document structure and retrieval evaluation.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Preserve headings, source locations and the context needed to interpret each chunk.
    - Vary chunk size and overlap on representative questions.
    - Measure retrieval misses and downstream answer quality, including table and boundary cases.
  - Read: [Contextual Retrieval in AI Systems](https://www.anthropic.com/news/contextual-retrieval) (Anthropic)
- **When would you combine lexical and dense retrieval, and how would you merge their rankings?**
  - Knowledge · Asked at: [Microsoft](../companies/microsoft.md) †, [Perplexity](../companies/perplexity.md) †
  - Tests: Whether exact terms and semantic similarity receive appropriate treatment.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Explain lexical strength on identifiers and dense strength on paraphrases.
    - Fuse rankings without assuming raw scores are comparable.
    - Ablate each retriever and reranking on a fixed relevance set.
  - Read: [Contextual Retrieval in AI Systems](https://www.anthropic.com/news/contextual-retrieval) (Anthropic)
- **Where should a cross-encoder reranker sit in a retrieval pipeline, and when does its quality gain justify latency?**
  - Knowledge · Asked at: [Microsoft](../companies/microsoft.md) †, [Perplexity](../companies/perplexity.md) †
  - Tests: Whether candidate count, recall and reranking cost are balanced.
- **How would you separately evaluate document retrieval and answer generation in a RAG application?**
  - Applied scenario
  - Tests: Whether failures can be attributed to the correct stage.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Build questions with relevant passages and acceptable answer criteria.
    - Measure retrieval recall separately from answer support and correctness.
    - Use oracle passages to distinguish retrieval failures from generation failures.
  - Read: [Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401) (Lewis et al., arXiv) · [Demystifying evals for AI agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/demystifying-evals-for-ai-agents) (Anthropic)
- **Explain hypothetical-document retrieval and how you would establish whether it improves your query distribution.**
  - Knowledge
  - Tests: Whether generated query expansion is treated as a testable hypothesis.
- **Search quality declines as the corpus changes. How would you detect embedding drift and separate it from indexing defects?**
  - Applied scenario
  - Tests: Whether diagnosis uses stable relevance sets and production slices.
- **Compare exact search, HNSW and IVF-PQ for an embedding index under memory, recall and latency constraints.**
  - Knowledge
  - Tests: Whether approximation is evaluated against a measurable exact baseline.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Use exact search on a sample as the recall baseline.
    - Compare graph traversal with coarse partitions and product quantisation.
    - Measure memory, update cost and filtered-search behaviour at target latency.
  - Read: [Efficient and robust approximate nearest neighbor search using Hierarchical Navigable Small World graphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.09320) (Malkov and Yashunin, arXiv) · [Faiss indexes](https://github.com/facebookresearch/faiss/wiki/Faiss-indexes) (Faiss maintainers)
- **How would you index tables, diagrams and multi-column pages without losing their relationships to surrounding text?**
  - System design
  - Tests: Whether parsing errors and layout structure are considered before embedding.
- **Design continuous index updates, including changed documents, deletions and queries during a rebuild.**
  - System design · Asked at: [Perplexity](../companies/perplexity.md) †
  - Tests: Whether freshness has consistency guarantees and an observable lag.
- **How would you connect each factual claim in an answer to the retrieved passage that supports it?**
  - System design · Asked at: [Perplexity](../companies/perplexity.md) †
  - Tests: Whether a citation is checked for support rather than merely attached.
- **A user asks for the count of open orders blocked by supplier issues. Why might document retrieval fail, and what should answer the query?**
  - Applied scenario · Asked at: [Palantir](../companies/palantir.md) †
  - Tests: Whether structured aggregation is separated from semantic retrieval.
- **How can a patient's existing medication list help transcribe drug names without causing the recogniser to insert drugs that were never spoken?**
  - Applied scenario
  - Tests: Whether contextual retrieval is balanced against confirmation bias.
